subject: biology-2
question: A garden plant has a diploid body with stems, leaves, and **flowers**, while its gametophyte survives as a few cells inside the flower, and its **seeds** develop inside **fruits**. Which group does this plant belong to, and which generation is dominant?

options.text: A moss, in which the gametophyte is dominant.
A fern, in which the sporophyte is dominant.
A conifer, in which the gametophyte is dominant.
An **angiosperm**, in which the **sporophyte** is dominant.

explanation: Seeds developing inside fruits are a defining feature of angiosperms, the most diverse group of land plants, whose visible body is the diploid sporophyte. The angiosperm gametophyte is reduced to a few cells nourished inside the flower, so A and C fail on both the group and the generation. B names a sporophyte-dominant group, but ferns release spores rather than seeds in fruits.
